title: Redwood Security Review - SSO/SCIM/RBAC - HorizonCare
summary: Security review focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC/least-privilege model for a pilot. Discussed SOC 2/ISO artifacts, audit log forwarding, data residency, and KMS/customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated. Agreed next steps: share SAML metadata template, SOC 2 report, RBAC mapping spreadsheet, and schedule a technical pilot for SCIM provisioning next week.

transcript_header: Date: 2026-07-15 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Maya P., Jordan L., Priya N. (Redwood); Sara T., Alan R., Nina K. (HorizonCare)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:06] Sara Thompson: Hi, Sara Thompson, CISO at HorizonCare. We're looking to lock down SSO and provisioning for a pilot.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, SE at Redwood. I'll walk through how SAML and SCIM work with our platform and then we can dig into RBAC.
[00:20] Dr. Alan Reyes: Alan, head of MLOps. Interested in how role separation works for model deployment.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Priya, security PM on Redwood side, I'll chime in on audit logs and compliance artifacts.
[00:35] (crosstalk)
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Great. High level: for hosted customers we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for user/group provisioning. For Dedicated/Private we support the same protocols plus options for on-prem SCIM proxies.
[00:55] Nina Kapoor: Quick Q - do you support Okta and Azure AD? We use Okta primarily but have some Azure AD for partners.
[01:03] Jordan Lee: Yes both Okta and Azure AD are first class. We map SCIM groups to Redwood roles. Common pattern: SCIM group "redwood-ops" => Operator role, "redwood-admins" => Admin.
[01:20] Sara Thompson: How do you do attribute mapping in SAML? We need the roles to be asserted in the SAML token.
[01:26] Jordan Lee: We support SAML attribute statements. You can send a "roles" attribute or groups. We recommend using groups for SCIM to avoid large SAML payloads. For Okta we typically set up group to attribute mapping and then SCIM does the heavy lifting.
[01:42] Dr. Alan Reyes: We want least privilege for MLOps - devs should not be able to change billing or access logs. How granular are the roles?
[01:50] Maya Patel: We have a built-in RBAC model: Admin, Model-Admin, Operator, Developer, Viewer, Billing. You can also create custom roles with explicit permissions per page/action.
[02:03] Jordan Lee: Right, and for pilot we usually recommend starting with three groups: Admin (1-2 people), Operator (platform ops), and Developer (MLOps engineers). Then add Model-Admin for model rollouts.
[02:17] Nina Kapoor: If SCIM is provisioning users, what's the sync cadence? We need near real-time offboarding.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: SCIM provisioning is near real-time - immediate create/update/delete events. Okta will push changes as they happen; our SCIM endpoint acknowledges and processes. For additional assurance we support periodic full-syncs and a manual reconciliation job.
[02:40] Priya Nair: On offboarding we also recommend using SCIM deprovision events to automatically revoke active sessions and invalidate long-lived tokens.
[02:49] Sara Thompson: Sessions - do you expose session logs and token revocation in the audit logs?
[02:54] Jordan Lee: Yes. Audit logs include session start/stop, token issuance/revocation, user role changes, and API key operations. We can stream logs to S3, CloudWatch, or a syslog endpoint for SIEM ingestion.
[03:10] Dr. Alan Reyes: Retention? Our compliance team requires 1 year of immutable logs, ideally exported to our SIEM.
[03:17] Priya Nair: For hosted customers we retain detailed audit logs for 90 days in the console UI and can provide exports for longer retention. For enterprise Dedicated/Private we offer configurable retention and the ability to ship logs to your SIEM for long-term archival.
[03:34] Nina Kapoor: Encryption - how is data encrypted at rest and in transit? Can we bring our own key?
[03:40] Jordan Lee: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS1.3. At rest we use AES-256. For hosted we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS integrations - AWS KMS or GCP KMS - and for Private we can integrate with your HSM.
[03:58] Sara Thompson: Does BYOK cover model artifacts and embeddings too?
[04:03] Jordan Lee: We can scope that in the pilot. Generally artifacts and customer data stored in object storage can be encrypted with your CMK. Model binaries we treat as part of the runtime image; for Private we can ensure they live on your infrastructure under your keys.
[04:18] (pause)
[04:25] Maya Patel: On compliance: we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. I'll share the reports after NDA.
[04:32] Sara Thompson: Great. We'll need the SOC2 report and an SOC2 assertion for security and privacy controls.
[04:38] Priya Nair: We'll also add a brief control mapping doc to show where Redwood controls align to your request for proposal controls.
[04:46] Dr. Alan Reyes: For SAML specifics - signing algorithms and cert rotation - are you flexible? Our IdP requires SHA256 and 365 day cert rotation.
[04:55] Jordan Lee: We support SHA256. Cert rotation is supported - the SAML metadata can present multiple certificates to allow overlapping rotation windows. We'll provide a metadata endpoint and a metadata XML file for your IdP team.
[05:10] Nina Kapoor: What about IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated flows? We need SP-initiated for redirect-based login from internal apps.
[05:17] Jordan Lee: Both supported. For SP-initiated we provide login URLs. For IdP-initiated the IdP passes the assertion. Either way we map attributes and then SCIM provisions groups as needed.
[05:28] Sara Thompson: Auditability - can you provide read-only access to logs for our auditors?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Yes, we can create a read-only role scoped to audit logs that you can assign to external auditors via SCIM group mapping so you don't have to create accounts manually.
[05:44] (background noise)
[05:48] Jordan Lee: A few operational notes - for Dedicated we recommend VPC peering and private endpoints for SCIM/SAML endpoints, and you can host SCIM proxy in your VPC if you want all traffic internal.
[06:00] Dr. Alan Reyes: For pilot we'd prefer Hosted with BYOK and SCIM via Okta. If that works we can do a short smoke test.
[06:07] Maya Patel: That is a common pilot. We can do hosted with BYOK and SCIM provisioning; we'll need your Okta test tenant details and a list of pilot users.
[06:18] Nina Kapoor: On RBAC mapping, can you share a template? We have multiple teams and want least privilege defaults.
[06:24] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. I'll send a spreadsheet with recommended mappings and example policies. It's also possible to create custom roles per permission bit, but start simple.
[06:33] Sara Thompson: Data residency - our patients are EU-based, need data stored in EU only. Is that possible?
[06:40] Priya Nair: We have EU regions for data residency. For hosted customers you can select region; for strict residency and audit requirements we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with region pinning.
[06:51] Dr. Alan Reyes: Any implications for latency if we pick EU region?
[06:56] Jordan Lee: Slight latency increase for US teams but within our SLOs for typical inference loads. For latency sensitive workloads you can deploy Dedicated capacity in EU to reduce tail latency.
[07:07] Sara Thompson: Anything else around legal/contractual controls - data processing agreements?
[07:12] Maya Patel: We have a standard DPA and can add Data Processing Addendum with EU SCCs. We'll have legal follow up once you indicate intent.
[07:21] Nina Kapoor: For the SCIM trial - what scope of attributes do you require? Email, givenName, familyName, groups?
[07:27] Jordan Lee: Minimum: userName (email), externalId (optional), givenName, familyName, active flag, and group membership. We also accept custom attributes if you need to map department or cost center.
[07:40] (short pause)
[07:43] Sara Thompson: Can you demo the deprovisioning flow - i.e., remove a user and automatically revoke sessions?
[07:49] Jordan Lee: We can demo that in the pilot. The deprovisioning event triggers token invalidation and session termination; we also emit an audit log entry.
[07:58] Dr. Alan Reyes: Regarding API keys, is there a separation between user tokens and service/service-account keys? We want to rotate service keys via CI.
[08:06] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have service accounts and user tokens. Service accounts are scoped with granular permissions and can be rotated via API. You can also require short-lived tokens via our token service.
[08:18] Maya Patel: Ok, let's recap actions and timeline. Jordan will send RBAC template and SAML metadata. I'll send SOC2/ISO and legal/DPA starter. Nina will provide Okta test creds. We aim to kick off SCIM pilot week of July 20.
[08:33] Sara Thompson: Sounds good. Anything else from Redwood?
[08:37] Priya Nair: We'll include a short control mapping doc and our audit log export options.
[08:42] Nina Kapoor: Thanks all, we'll get the Okta tenant details over.
[08:45] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by Friday.
[08:49] (meeting ends)
